WebSocket is a first-class surface now, from the capture to the replay. Agents driving Ngintip over MCP can look at a flow instead of reading it. Passive scan waits to be asked. And a set of records that quietly said the wrong thing now say what actually happened.

## Nothing to do before upgrading

Unlike 0.3.0, this one needs no action from you.

- **Project files are compatible both ways.** A `.ngintip` from 0.3.x opens here, and one saved here opens in 0.3.x minus the columns it does not know about. The new `unsent` column is added by migration on first open.
- **No MCP contract changes.** 31 tools become 32. One is added, none changed, none removed, so your agent config keeps working untouched.
- **No CA regeneration**, no listener migration, nothing to re-trust.

## Two things worth knowing

**Ngintip now gives up after 180 seconds.** Previous versions waited for as long as the client did, forever if the client was patient. The default is now a three minute deadline on the response, in **Settings > Project > Performance**. Set it to 0 to go back to waiting indefinitely. If you test endpoints that legitimately take longer than three minutes, change this first.

**`history_image` needs the app window open.** The evidence card is drawn in the webview, so the one card layout serves both the window and MCP. An agent calling it against a headless Ngintip gets a clear error rather than a second, subtly different card.

---

## WebSocket, end to end

History separates HTTP from WS with a switch, and the WS segment carries the socket count. A flow is recognised as a socket by its **101** status rather than by its path, so a handshake on `/api/v2/stream` is found like one on `/ws`. The detail pane lists frames with direction, opcode and timing, and renders binary ones as a hex dump.

**Repeater has socket tabs.** Connect, send text, binary, ping or pong, watch the frames arrive, and send again on the same connection. A frame in the log can be edited and resent in one click, including a binary one, which is read back out of its hex dump. The toolbar says what the connection is doing in words: not connected, connecting, open, closed, and who closed it.

A handshake sent to Repeater from anywhere now opens as a socket tab instead of a request that could never work. An HTTP tab already holding one converts in place with **Open as socket**.

Three ways a socket used to leak are closed: a close from the server side is visible instead of silent, closing a tab closes its connection, and connections orphaned by a window reload are swept at startup.

Organizer records carry their WebSocket frames. Records written by earlier versions are unchanged and still read.

## Evidence cards over MCP

`history_image` draws a flow as a card an agent can actually see: method, URL, status, duration and the message bodies, coloured per token. It returns an image, not a description of one, so the agent reviewing a finding looks at the same thing you would.

## Passive scan waits to be asked

The scan that used to start itself on every launch is gone. The empty state now carries the button that starts one, and the button says how many flows it is about to read. A scan reads the body of every captured flow, so on a project of a few thousand that was a surprise that arrived by itself; now it is a decision.

**In scope only** is on by default. With no scope set, everything is in scope and nothing is skipped.

**Clear** is now **Delete all**, and it deletes both the findings and the record of which flows were read, so a later scan finds them again. If you want one finding to stay gone, delete it with Select, or delete its flow from History. The dialog says so.

## Extensions know which flow they are working on

`ctx.flow_id` is filled at every stage and on every surface that has a row behind it: proxied traffic, a message held in the interceptor, a stored flow being decoded for display, and `repeater_send` over MCP. Previously `process_*` knew it on the proxy but the `decode_*` and `encode_*` hooks over the same bytes were handed nothing, and the one replay surface that does write a History row was the one that gave `None`. `ctx.path` is filled on the replay surfaces too.

**A hook that only reads a message no longer marks its flow as edited.** The runner answered a hook that returned nothing by re-serializing the message, which changed line endings and recomputed `Content-Length`, and the host decides "edited" by comparing bytes. One logging extension was enough to put Original and Final tabs on every row in History and make the Modified column meaningless. If you have been seeing that, it stops here.

**Hooks are scanned from the file the worker runs**, not from the copy saved beside it. Editing a script on disk without saving the extension list again used to mean a newly added hook was never called, with nothing in the log to say why.

## Records that say what actually happened

**History holds the request that really went upstream.** An extension's `process_request` edits the outgoing message in place, but the row was built before that ran. The header your hook added crossed the wire and then appeared nowhere, and Original held the same text as Final. Both tabs now show their own version.

**A request the target never saw says so.** A client that gives up while Ngintip is still running an extension hook used to leave no trace at all. It is now recorded, and marked as never sent, which is a different finding from a request the target received and answered into a connection that had already closed. The table shows it as `UNSENT`.

**Rows no longer flatten four situations into one.** Waiting, late, no answer filed, and an observed failure are separate states, and only the last is red. A healthy request still out at the target used to look exactly like a dead one.

## Also

- A body capped at the 256 KB view limit keeps **Pretty**. It used to lose it at exactly the size where reading one unformatted line is hopeless, because the cut usually lands mid-string and the parse fails.
- **Beautify copies text nodes byte for byte** instead of collapsing the spaces inside them. It runs on what Repeater and Intercept send, so it was quietly altering signed bodies and any value whose spacing matters. `<pw> secret </pw>` stays as typed.
- Large projects open without the window stalling, and History tails without spending most of a frame redrawing forty visible rows.
- A toast no longer cancels the one after it.
- Selection actions, a WebSocket-aware search, and a decoder that reads a socket frame.

---

## Verifying your download

`SHA256SUMS.txt` is attached. On macOS and Linux:

```
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing
```

On Windows:

```
Get-FileHash .\Ngintip_0.4.0_x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```
